newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London steady, trading volume light.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London steady, trading volume light.

text.p: U.S. shares were steady on Tuesday with many European investors reluctant to take new positions ahead of key U.S. unemployment figures due at the end of the week.
"Many people think the Fed will push up rates next month. If we get a strong jobs number, the fear of a hike will grow," another dealer said.

A slim majority of economists contacted by Reuters believe the U.S. Federal Reserve will increase its short-term funds rate to 5.75 percent from the current 5.25 percent at the next FOMC meeting on July 1 and 2.
Twenty of 37 economists surveyed by Reuters on Friday and Monday said they expected to bank to lift its key rate amid signs of a tight labour market and strong consumer demand.
The Fed last raised its funds rate by 25 basis points on March 25.
Dealers here expect the Dow Industrials, which fell nearly 42 points on Monday to close at 7,289.40, to start steady, supported by a firm bond market.
The June T-bond was up 1/32 to 110-7/32 while the yield on the benchmark 30-year long bond stood at 6.90 percent by 1015 GMT.

Chrysler Corp was $3/8 to $31-3/4 after the company said on Monday sales fell by 16.6 percent in May from a record month in 1996 due to weaker consumer demand and an engine plant strike that curtailed truck and jeep production.
Ford Motor Co rose $1/4 to $37-1/2 following a report in the Wall Street Journal which said the company was poised to post record quarterly profits.

Elsewhere, Coca Cola Co added $1/8 to $67-3/4 after press reports said the company had offered McDonalds Corp franchisees incentives in order to secure an exclusive right to sell its products in the fast-food giant's thousands of U.S. restaurants.
